examples.solution_text:
(a) The HCF is $7$. Divide both terms by $7$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}14u+21\\&=7\left(\frac{14u}{7}+\frac{21}{7}\right)\\&=7(2u+3)\end{aligned}$
(b) The HCF is $6$. Keep the subtraction sign.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}18v-30\\&=6\left(\frac{18v}{6}-\frac{30}{6}\right)\\&=6(3v-5)\end{aligned}$

(a) Both terms have a factor of $s$. Dividing each term by $s$ gives $8t$ and $5$.
$8st+5s=s(8t+5)$
Check: $s(8t+5)=8st+5s$.
(b) The numerical HCF is $4$. Both terms contain $r^2$, the lower power. The HCF is $4r^2$.
Divide each term by $4r^2$: the results are $4r$ and $-7$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}16r^3-28r^2\\&=4r^2(4r-7)\end{aligned}$
Check: $4r^2(4r-7)=16r^3-28r^2$.

The HCF of all three terms is $5$. Divide each term by $5$.
$\begin{aligned}15a\div5&=3a\\-25b\div5&=-5b\\5\div5&=1\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}15a-25b+5\\&=5(3a-5b+1)\end{aligned}$
Keep the $1$: expanding $5\times1$ returns the last term $5$.

examples.question_text:
Leah wrote $30c-42d=3(10c-14d)$.
(a) Explain why this is not fully factorised and write the fully factorised form.
(b) Expand your result to check it.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The terms inside $10c-14d$ still share a factor of $2$. The HCF of the original terms is $6$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}30c-42d\\&=6(5c-7d)\end{aligned}$
The terms $5c$ and $-7d$ share no common factor other than $1$.
(b) Multiply $6$ by each term.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}6(5c-7d)\\&=6(5c)-6(7d)\\&=30c-42d\end{aligned}$
This is the original expression.

examples.derivation: HCF(14,21)=7; dividing gives 2u and 3, hence 7(2u+3). HCF(18,30)=6; dividing gives 3v and -5, hence 6(3v-5). Both expand to their original expressions. These adapt the numerical-factor examples at source lines 89–98 and 237–255.

The common algebraic factor of 8st and 5s is s, giving s(8t+5). HCF(16,28)=4 and the lowest shared power is r^2; division by 4r^2 gives 4r and -7, hence 4r^2(4r-7). Both expansion checks are correct. The method follows source lines 446–483 and the shared-power exercises at 497–507.
HCF(15,25,5)=5. The three quotients are 3a, -5b and 1, giving 5(3a-5b+1). Expansion returns 15a-25b+5. This adapts the three-term numerical-factor exercises at source lines 308–310.

3(10c-14d) is equivalent to the original expression but its bracket retains a factor of 2. HCF(30,42)=6, giving 6(5c-7d). The remaining terms have no non-unit common factor. Expansion gives 30c-42d.
